branch_provenance.syndrome: Chronic Progressive Focal Sweating Disorder of Uncertain Aetiology

state.case_summary:
A 31-year-old male nursing student with a history of axillary hyperhidrosis presented with excessive sweating of the buttocks, most severe at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum. He had previously treated his axillary condition successfully with 20% aluminum chloride; however, treatment of the intergluteal cleft and sacrum with aluminum chloride was unsuccessful. Due to the severity of the condition, he used absorbent pads yet continued to soak through his pants and was consequently unable to attend work.

The Minor starch-iodine test was performed to help localize the sites of overactive sweating. Areas of significant sweating were identified in the sacral region (10 × 3-cm area) and intergluteal cleft (6 × 8-cm area).

- Clinical Tests:    Test Name: Minor starch-iodine test    Purpose: To localize areas of excessive sweating    Results: Identified areas of significant sweating in the sacral and intergluteal regions    - Visual Documentation:    Image Title: Grid Markings on the Sacrum and Intergluteal Cleft    Image Description: A 10 × 3-cm grid was drawn on the sacrum and a 6 × 8-cm grid was drawn on the intergluteal cleft, with the outermost dots omitted
